blocks.title: How a Power Grid Balances Supply and Demand
items: Plants **feed** electricity into the grid; output must **match demand second by second**.
**High-voltage lines** carry power over long distances with **low losses**; **substations** step the voltage down.
Demand **peaks in the early evening**; operators call on **fast-ramping** plants to **meet the peak**.
Grid frequency is held at **50 or 60 Hz**; a **sustained deviation** signals imbalance and can **trigger protective shutdowns**.
Batteries **absorb** surplus and **release** it when demand **spikes**, **smoothing** the curve.
Operators plan for the **loss of the largest unit** (the “N-1 rule”), so a single failure does not **cascade**.
blocks.note: Figures vary by country; the principle of continuous balancing is universal.

body: **Keep the lights on.** — Manter tudo funcionando.
**Pull the plug.** — Desligar, encerrar.
**Under strain.** — Sob pressão.
**At full stretch.** — No limite da capacidade.
**Run out of steam.** — Perder o fôlego.
**Down the line.** — Mais adiante.
**Plug the gap.** — Tapar a lacuna.
**Blow a fuse.** — Perder a paciência.
**Live wire.** — Pessoa enérgica.
**Safety net.** — Rede de segurança.
**Demand peaks at six o’clock.** — A demanda atinge o pico às seis.
**And if the largest unit fails?** — E se a maior unidade falhar?
**The N-1 rule keeps the grid stable.** — A regra N-1 mantém a rede estável.
